summary.headline: Sundrop Brands Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY with EBITDA margin steady at about 7%, gross margin up ~110 bps.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY and 11% QoQ, with B2B up 18% and e-commerce up 32%. Sundrop business (about 56% of sales) grew 16% and Del Monte (about 44-45%) grew 14%. Gross margin improved about 110 bps despite commodity and packaging inflation, and EBITDA margin held at about 7% (about 5.66% after ESOP cost as management cited on the call). Management said A&P spends fell about 12% YoY as reported, or about 5% on a like-for-like basis after reclassifying trade spends.

financial_highlights.value: Down about 12% YoY as reported; about 5% lower like-for-like (21.4% vs 22.9% of sales)

segments.name: Popcorn
segments.commentary: Growing about 18% in value with about 12% volume growth; management claims about 85% category share. Ready-to-Eat growing about 39% (from 33% last year) while Ready-to-Cook grows about 9%.

segments.name: Culinary (ketchup, mayo, dressings)
segments.commentary: Value growth accelerated to 15% from about 10% last year, with volume around 8%. Mix of retail and B2B, with B2B growing strongly and some exports to Southeast Asia.

segments.name: Premium staples / edible oil
segments.commentary: Value growth about 16% with volume about 7%; about 9 points of the value growth attributed to price pass-through. Management targets 4-5% volume growth.

segments.name: Italian (olive oil, pasta, RTE olives)
segments.commentary: Volume up about 15-17% and value up about 8%, the first value growth in this business after a year of deflation-driven declines. Olive oil volume grew close to 20%; pasta grew about 10%.

segments.name: Peanut butter / spreads
segments.commentary: Still declining, though improved to about -3% in value and volume from -8% to -10% last year. Share is about 33% in standard peanut butter and about 3% in value-added variants.

guidance_outlook: Management targets mid-teens to high-teens growth, with growth split roughly 50% volume, 25% price and 25% innovation over the long term.
Ambition to lift EBITDA margin about 300 bps a year, half reinvested in the business and half returned to shareholders; target of about 12% margin in three years (FY30).
Synergies from Sundrop-Del Monte integration estimated at about 200 bps, to be delivered over about 18 months.
ESOP cost is front-loaded and expected to continue for another 18-21 months, after which it becomes marginal to the P&L (about 100 bps benefit).
Italian business value growth expected to approach about 15% if volume growth of 15% is sustained; Italian price realisation to stabilise from Q2.
Innovation expected to contribute about 6-8% of growth; innovation currently at about 6% of sales from roughly 100 products launched in the last 24 months.
capex_capacity: Capital-efficient model adopted over the last two years: use of third-party manufacturing alongside own assets, with focus on utilisation of existing capacity.
Popcorn facilities at Kashipur and Kothur are improving utilisation, adding to profitability of instant popcorn; Ready-to-Eat Rs.10 packs are assorted-manufactured.
Distribution consolidation: Del Monte has 10 unique CFAs, with about 2 consolidated and a third underway; target of about 8 consolidations by end of this year, leaving 2 unique CFAs for Del Monte.
ERP evaluation under way for a single ERP across both organisations, with migration planned within about 12 months; sales force consolidation to follow.
About 80% of outlets now billed through the automated sales-force platform, up from about 75% at end of Q4.
demand_pricing: Price pass-through is being used heavily: in edible oil, about 9 points of 15% value growth came from price, per management, with per-kg price increases passed through.
Italian realisation fell 6-10% last year on commodity deflation; price pass-out began in Q2 last year, so Q1 still carried higher-cost inventory.

Peanut butter shifted to value-added formats (chocolate, high-protein, natural) that took about 85% of the category; Sundrop has about 3% share there. E-commerce in peanut butter has returned to about 16% growth.
Ready-to-Eat growth driven by distribution expansion in general trade; strongest in North, then East, with West and South under development. E-commerce Rs.25-50 packs are driving growth.
Management said competition from new-age, digitally led peanut butter brands is intense, and the company will invest in digital consumer acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: Is the A&P decline a result of greater efficiency or a change in focus?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it dropped the juices portfolio and kept investing in core categories; like-for-like A&P was 21.4% vs 22.9% of sales, about 5% lower after trade-spend reclassification.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Italian realisation fall due to quick-commerce discounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Kapoor said no; the drop reflected commodity deflation passed through to consumers in 2025, with pricing now stabilising and price pass-out from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How much of edible oil's 15% value growth is price?
qa_highlights.answer: Asheesh Kumar Sharma said about 9% came from price pass-through and about 7% from volume, with per-kg increases passed on in full.

qa_highlights.question: What is the synergy and timeline for the Sundrop-Del Monte merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about 200 bps of synergy over 18 months, with CFA consolidation by year-end and a single ERP within about 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path from about 7% EBITDA to about 12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management outlined about 100 bps from ESOP roll-off, about 200 bps from synergies, and further gains from scale and premiumisation to reach about 12% in three years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.10 Ready-to-Eat pack margin-sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.10 packs have turned margin-accretive over the last 18 months; bigger packs are about one-third of RTE sales and growing faster.

risks_watch: Commodity and packaging inflation (sunflower oil cited as running ahead of others) could hit volumes in premium staples if price increases are needed.
Peanut butter remains negative, and competition from digitally led, new-age brands in value-added formats is intense.
ESOP costs weigh on reported EBITDA for about 18-21 months.
Italian value recovery depends on sustaining about 15% volume growth.
Synergy and ERP timelines (about 12 months for ERP; 18 months for 200 bps synergy) need to be tracked.
Reclassification of trade spends makes A&P comparisons hard; watch like-for-like disclosures.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and margins, with direct explanations of the Italian and peanut butter weak spots and a clear time-bound plan. Management was less specific on the bridge from 7% to 12% EBITDA margin and on the Q1 margin split.
key_quotes: we have closed the quarter with a very stable, healthy EBITDA margins of 7%, which is what we also have achieved very similar number in Quarter 4 of last year.
Our overall endeavor is to improve our margins by 300 basis points every year, of which we would want to deploy half back to the business and half back to the shareholders.
We have about 33% share in the standard Peanut Butter market. We have a 3% share in the value-added Peanut Butter market.
Historically, our Ready-to-Eat Rs. 10 was a dilutive to margin business. But over the last 18 months, we have actually made it accretive to our margin business.

growth.why: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 15% YoY with mid-teens to high-teens long-term growth targeted (50% volume, 25% price, 25% innovation) and ~200 bps synergy from Sundrop-Del Monte integration over 18 months, but no new capacity additions were quantified; the asset-light model and rising popcorn plant utilisation are the only supply-side backing, and there is no EBITDA growth figure stated.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management targets about 300 bps a year and about 12% EBITDA margin by FY30 from ~7% now, with ~100 bps from ESOP roll-off over 18-21 months and ~200 bps from Sundrop-Del Monte synergies over 18 months; gross margin already up ~110 bps YoY, though the Q1 margin bridge was not clear.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new capacity quantified; company is asset-light (third-party manufacturing) and Kashipur/Kothur popcorn plants are improving utilisation from existing headroom, so no new plant is signalled in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Popcorn volume about 12%, Culinary volume about 8%, Italian volume 15-17%, premium staples/edible oil volume about 7% with a 4-5% target; but price contributed about 9 points of edible oil's 15% value growth, so volume is partly price-masked.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management stresses a capital-efficient model with third-party manufacturing and utilisation of existing assets; no capex amount, land or board approval mentioned, and utilisation level not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY and 11% QoQ, with e-commerce up 32%, Italian volume up 15-17%, and Culinary value up 15%, so the mid-teens to high-teens growth target looks achievable, though no explicit guidance raise was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Sunflower oil and packaging inflation could force price increases that hit premium staples volumes, and Italian value recovery depends on sustaining about 15% volume growth; peanut butter still at about -3% value growth.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: About 100 products launched in the last 24 months with innovation at ~6% of sales, and management targets innovation contributing 6-8% of growth; no specific named launch dated.

rows.label: Sundrop-Del Monte distribution and ERP consolidation
rows.when: CFA consolidation by year-end; ERP within ~12 months
rows.why: Del Monte has 10 unique CFAs with about 2 consolidated and a third underway, targeting about 8 consolidations by year-end, and a single ERP within about 12 months, feeding the ~200 bps synergy over 18 months.

rows.label: Italian price realisation stabilises from Q2
rows.why: Price pass-out began in Q2 last year after 6-10% realisation declines, and management expects Italian value growth to approach about 15% if 15% volume growth is sustained.

rows.label: ESOP cost roll-off
rows.why: ESOP cost is front-loaded and expected to run another 18-21 months before becoming marginal, worth about 100 bps of EBITDA margin benefit.
